args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service was failing health checks with an error rate of ~18%. The release candidate v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is ~0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. All three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) now run v2.3.0. The service passes health checks and the error rate is about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 is open as a SEV2 for checkout-api, and the on-call engineer has been paged. It describes the failure, the rollback and the result. It also notes that the test version of v2.3.1 was already unhealthy in staging before it went to production. The root cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before it's redeployed.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
